title: Research sprint digest — quant + evals (Apr 4 2027)
content:
Sprint window: 2027-03-21 -> 2027-04-04
Attendees (weekly sync): Aisha (owner), Marco (quant lead), Lina (evals), Owen (runtime), Priya (onboarding) + ad-hoc: Deb, Sanjay

Purpose: capture finished experiments, quick wins, regressions, and next actions for model-onboarding + quantization + eval surface. This is a working digest; notes are rough and include TODOs and follow-ups.

High level summary:
- We ran a focused set of quantization experiments across 3 models (open-7b-v2, opt-6.7-lite, and a customer POC family) with q4 variants, q8 mixed, and a small float fallback. Overall outcome: q4_r variant gives the best latency/cost tradeoff for short-context low-latency workloads; q4_0 had slightly better perplexity on long-context summarization but increased memory pressure and KV-cache thrash.
- Eval suite (Lina) added two new probes: token-coherence (hallucination detector) and long-context rolling-rouge for chain-of-thought style tasks. Early signal: quantized models increase token-level hallucination rate by ~3–5% on the token-coherence probe for open-7b-v2 at 4k context.
- Onboarding: Priya verified packaging flow for "open-7b-v2-q4r" and created canary configs in the Dedicated test pool (small). Canary rollout scheduled next week.

Experiment details (short):
1) q4 variants: q4_0 vs q4_r on open-7b-v2
   - throughput (tokens/s) at batch size 8, seq=512: q4_r +28% vs baseline fp16; q4_0 +32% but with 12% higher tail latency (p95) during cache writes.
   - avg GPU mem: q4_r reduced mem by ~36% vs fp16, enabling 1.5x density on current A10 pools.
   - quality: ROUGE-L on summarization dev set: fp16=0.41, q4_r=0.397, q4_0=0.401. Token-coherence fail rate: fp16=4.1%, q4_r=7.2%, q4_0=6.4% (note: higher for q4_r in this run for reasons below).
   - observation: q4_r decode math shows more variance on KV-cache hotpaths, likely due to alignment on attention kernels under quant rounding.

2) long-context (4k) runs:
   - q4 variants show higher perplexity drift over sequence length; for open-7b-v2 the difference becomes noticeable after token 2500 (avg logprob drop).
   - We tried chunked KV-refresh heuristics in runtime: short-term fix reduced drift by ~40% for q4_r but introduced slight latency p95 increase at high QPS.

3) opt-6.7-lite (customer POC):
   - Quantized mixed (q8 for attention, q4 for MLP) gave stable hallucination numbers and 22% latency improvement. This mixed strategy might be a good default for customer POCs who care about semantic fidelity.

Runtime/infra notes (Owen):
- KV cache write contention surfaced when we increased concurrency in the Dedicated test pool. Repro steps: replay multi-session workload with long-prefix warmups -> p95 spikes on cache write path.
- Temporary mitigation: bump KV cache lock sharding from 4 -> 12 shards. This reduced p95 spikes in canary by ~18%. Longer-term: implement lock-free append queue (tracking issue opened).

Eval notes (Lina):
- New token-coherence probe: synthetic prompts + adversarial distractor sentences to stress hallucination. Running on larger eval corpus next week (20k prompts).
- Human eval pilot: 200 samples across models; early signal is that humans prefer fp16 outputs for nuanced summarization (~60% pref). Need larger sample to be conclusive.

Model onboarding (Priya):
- Packaging checklist added to repo: model-config.json, quant-metadata, compatibility matrix (kernel requirements).
- Canary plan: 5% of Dedicated test pool traffic -> monitor latency, cost, quality via existing dashboards. Rollback on any regression beyond thresholds (p95 +20% or token-coherence +3pp).

Decisions made in sync:
- Default inference profile for low-latency hosted customers: q4_r (canary) + runtime KV-shard bump. Rationale: consistent latency gains, predictable memory, manageable quality tradeoffs for short-context tasks.
- For long-context and high-fidelity products, recommend mixed quant (q8 attention + q4 MLP) or keep fp16; add these as named profiles in the model catalog.

Open questions / risks:
- Why did q4_r fail token-coherence more than q4_0 in the first open-7b-v2 run? Hypothesis: rounding/rescaling differences + different kernel ordering; need kernel-level trace. Action: Marco to profile with per-layer logits delta tracing (JIRA-ML-1291).
- Impact on A/B experiments: small human pref delta in pilot — is that signal noisy or real? Lina to expand human eval N to 1k.
- Long-sequence drift mitigation tradeoffs between latency and quality — how far can we push KV-refresh heuristics before p95 cost is unacceptable? Owen to simulate via load tests.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Marco: run per-layer quant-trace for open-7b-v2 q4_r vs q4_0, attach diffs to PR #742 (ETA 2027-04-10).
- Lina: run expanded token-coherence eval on 20k prompts and human N=1k; produce summary (ETA 2027-04-18).
- Priya: start canary for open-7b-v2-q4r in Dedicated small pool, monitor first 72h, report (ETA kickoff 2027-04-11).
- Owen: implement lock-free append queue spike prototype; if not feasible, land permanent KV-shard config (ETA spike prototype 2027-04-22, fallback config earlier).
- Aisha: update model catalog entries with new profiles and canary rollout checklist (ETA 2027-04-12).

Notes to self / miscellaneous:
- Add a short README for quant metadata format (schema) — we keep changing field names across PRs.
- Consider a short-term perf knob in hosted API to prefer mixed-quant profile for queries > 2k tokens.
- Revisit pricing guidance for quant profiles once cost per-token delta is stable across 2 weeks of canary.

Meeting snippets / unresolved threads: 
- Slack thread #quant-playbook: Marco asked whether we should auto-switch to fp16 after 3k tokens; consensus unclear. Tagging ops for rate-limiting impacts.
- Architecture PR #717 (kernel selection) is blocked on compatibility tests on Ampere gen vs older GPUs — reassign to infra for smoke tests.

End of digest. Will update after the first 72h of canary and Marco's layer-traces come in.

Quick search refs: model names in this note are internal shorthand; real model-artifacts live in git LFS under gh:/models/catalog.

-- aisha
